text:
Anika: Quick UX check — the new entry gateway rail (left-side slim rail) vs the flyout modal: which one actually reduces cognitive load for first-time users? I sat with 3 test users and they clicked the banner but expected an immediate checklist, not a full modal.
Sam: saw that too in the usability lab. Rail feels lighter but people miss the checklist affordance. The flyout forces a flow, but it's heavier and blocks exploration.
Raj: my concern is metrics: our convert-to-try rate dropped when we switched to the rail in the last experiment. Might be because the CTA label is ambiguous: "Start" vs "Set up workspace" vs "Try sample". Suggest A/B copy only.
Julia: accessibility nits from the audit — the rail's CTA contrast is 3.8:1 on the default theme (fails AA). Also keyboard focus order jumps from nav to body, skipping the rail CTA. Needs tabindex fix.
Anika: good point. For copy: test the hypothesis that explicit intent works better. Proposed CTAs: 1) "Create demo project" 2) "Follow setup checklist" 3) "Try a sample stack" — shorter vs explicit.
Sam: +1 for explicit. Microcopy under CTA could be 1-line: "Create a sandbox with prebuilt prompts and examples — 2 minutes." Low friction.
Raj: operational note: if we push users into a modal checklist we should respect canary flows for Dedicated customers — sticky preference saved in profile. Otherwise we annoy returning users.
Julia: a11y checklist: ensure the rail has role="region" and aria-label, add visible focus ring, and make CTA reachable with single Tab from the top nav. Also increase contrast to >=4.5:1. I'll paste the quick fixes:
```
.rail-cta {
  outline: 3px solid var(--focus-color);
  color: #0b2a66; /* darker */
}
``` 
DesignBot: Figma link updated by @Julia — https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/entry-gateway-rail — version 4 has contrast tweaks and two copy variants.
Anika: Decision proposal: keep rail as default for low-friction discoverability, but change CTA copy to "Create demo project" and add a subtle inline checklist preview (3 bullets) so users know what to expect. If they click "Full setup" open the flyout modal with the step-by-step checklist.
Sam: that hybrid seems promising — inline preview reduces surprise, modal preserves guided flow. We should add telemetry: event names: `entry_rail_cta_click`, `entry_flyout_open`, `entry_preview_expand`.
Raj: agree. Also add an experiment to test sticky dismiss: if a user dismisses the rail once, don't show for 14 days. Track `entry_rail_dismiss`.
Julia: I'll upload updated components and a keyboard-nav spec. Small UX ask: change the preview bullet text to be action-oriented ("Invite a teammate", "Deploy sample app", "Run a test prompt").
Anika: can we get design and eng estimate? If it's under 2 days we can include in next sprint, otherwise schedule for the one after.
Sam: engineering: estimate ~3 days (rail copy + contrast + tabindex + telemetry). Modal flyout is existing component so hooking it up is small. I'll create a ticket.
Julia: I'll drop the Figma prototype and a11y checklist in the ticket. Also capturing contrast numbers and voiceover notes.
Anika: thanks — let's reconvene after the experiment plan is in the ticket. :thumbsup:
